chunks: One is that we say: Since it is established that the necessity of Imamate is in every state, and that the creation, being fallible, cannot be without a leader at any time, and that a condition of the leader is that he be ascertained to be infallible,
then that leader is either manifest and known, or hidden and concealed,

when we know that everyone who claims for him a manifest Imamate is not ascertained to be infallible, rather the outward appearance of their actions and states contradicts infallibility, we know that he who is ascertained to be infallible is hidden and concealed.

and when we know that everyone who claims for him infallibility absolutely, who is hidden, such as the Kaisaniyya, Nawusiyya, Fatihiyya, Waqifiyya and others, their claim is false, we know by this the validity of the Imamate of the son of Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and the validity of his occultation and guardianship,

and we do not need to exert in speech regarding the proof of his birth, and the reason for his occultation, given the establishment of what we mentioned, because the truth cannot be absent from the community.
ai.seo_question: What is the theological proof for the occultation of Imam Mahdi (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi employs a rigorous logical deduction (istidlal) to prove the necessity of a continuous, infallible Imam (Imamat al-Dahr) by eliminating all other possibilities. He argues that since visible claimants fail the test of infallibility and known hidden sects are erroneous, the true Imam must be the concealed son of Al-Hasan al-Askari, whose existence is guaranteed by the principle that divine truth cannot be absent from the community.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: One is that we say: Since it is proved that there must be an Imam in every age, and it is not possible that the people, being fallible, at any given time be without a chief, and that the chief must be ascertained to be infallible,
and that such a chief is either manifest and known or hidden and unknown,

and likewise it is clear that all those for whom a manifest Imamate is claimed, their infallibility is not ascertained, on the contrary the outward appearance of their actions contradicts infallibility, it is inferred that the infallible Imam, who must exist in every age, is (at present) hidden and invisible.

Likewise, taking into consideration that all those for whom infallibility is claimed, and are said to be invisible and hidden, such as the supposed hidden leaders of Kaisaniyya, Nawusiyya, Fatihiyya, Waqifiyya and others sects, their claims are invalid, thus the Imamate of the son of Imam Hasan Askari (a.s) and his occultation and mastership (Wilayah) is proved,

no other dispute is there in the Ummah. Hence, there is no need to take the burden of proving his birth and to explain the reasons of his occultation as the word of truth and true belief is present in the Ummah and not outside it.
